summary:
SMS Posen was a German Nassau-class battleship, commissioned in 1910 and among the first dreadnoughts built for the Imperial Navy. It carried twelve 28 cm guns in six twin turrets, arranged unusually around the ship’s sides, and was powered by triple-expansion engines.

During World War I, Posen served mainly in the North Sea, taking part in fleet sorties and the Battle of Jutland on 31 May–1 June 1916. In night fighting, it accidentally rammed the light cruiser SMS Elbing, which was badly damaged and later scuttled. Posen also operated in the Baltic. In August 1915, it helped German forces enter the Gulf of Riga, where it engaged Russian gunboats and the battleship Slava. In 1918, it returned to the Baltic to support White Finnish forces during Finland’s civil war.

Posen remained in Germany at the war’s end. Britain received it in 1919 as a replacement for ships scuttled at Scapa Flow. It was sold for scrapping in the Netherlands and broken up in 1922.
